[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Introduction to NoSQL Databases with MongoDB and Python"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"NoSQL databases offer a flexible alternative to traditional relational databases. MongoDB, a popular NoSQL database, stores data in JSON-like documents, making it well-suited for applications with evolving data structures. This tutorial will guide you through using MongoDB with Python."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Setting up MongoDB"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before you begin, ensure you have MongoDB installed and running. You can download MongoDB from the official website (mongodb.com) and follow the installation instructions for your operating system. Also, make sure the MongoDB server is running on the default port (27017) or configure your connection accordingly."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Installing the PyMongo Driver"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"To interact with MongoDB from Python, you'll need the PyMongo driver. Install it using pip:"},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"pip install pymongo"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Connecting to MongoDB"},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"from pymongo import MongoClient

client = MongoClient('mongodb://localhost:27017/') # Connect to MongoDB server
db = client['mydatabase'] # Access/Create a database named 'mydatabase'"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"This code establishes a connection to the MongoDB server running on localhost at port 27017. It then accesses (or creates if it doesn't exist) a database named 'mydatabase'."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Inserting Documents"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"collection = db['mycollection'] # Access/Create a collection named 'mycollection'

data = {
    'name': 'John Doe',
    'age': 30,
    'city': 'New York'
}

inserted_id = collection.insert_one(data).inserted_id
print(f'Inserted document with ID: {inserted_id}')"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"This code accesses (or creates) a collection named 'mycollection' within the 'mydatabase' database. It then inserts a document (a Python dictionary) into the collection and prints the ID of the inserted document."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Querying Documents"},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"for document in collection.find():
    print(document)

# Query with a filter
for document in collection.find({'age': {'$gt': 25}}):
    print(document)"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"The first loop iterates through all documents in the collection and prints each one. The second loop uses a filter to find documents where the 'age' field is greater than 25."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Updating Documents"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"collection.update_one(
    {'name': 'John Doe'},
    {'$set': {'city': 'Los Angeles'}}
)

print('Document updated successfully')"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"This code updates the first document where the 'name' field is 'John Doe', setting the 'city' field to 'Los Angeles'."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Deleting Documents"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"collection.delete_one({'name': 'John Doe'})

print('Document deleted successfully')"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"This code deletes the first document where the 'name' field is 'John Doe'."},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a basic introduction to using MongoDB with Python. You can explore more advanced features like indexing, aggregation, and replica sets in the MongoDB documentation. Remember to handle exceptions and properly close connections in your production code."}]
